comparator.name: UCU Liberal Arts and Sciences
comparator.route: Bachelor of Arts with an interdomain Humanities and Social Sciences major
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations set a 180 EC degree with at least 45 EC at level 3. This example shows a Humanities and Social Sciences interdomain BA. It allocates the 75 EC major minimum, including the 15 EC thesis, and shows both domains’ methods separately. The remaining choice space can change if approved methods overlap or the student takes more major courses.

alternatives.label: Society, culture & science
alternatives.concept: Combine politics, economics and sociology with history, philosophy and art to ask how societies respond to problems such as environmental change and health inequality. Develop statistical and qualitative research skills alongside science and cultural analysis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum distributes substantial study across society, culture and science, with economics, politics, sociology, philosophy, history, ecology, health and research methods; the label therefore names all three major domains.
progression: Early study of economics, life science, philosophy and research design supports later work in social theory, sustainability governance and health psychology. Qualitative methods precede advanced historical inquiry.

alternatives.label: Society, power & culture
alternatives.concept: Study how laws, political institutions and cultural representations shape power and inequality. Use historical sources, social research, literature, art and media to examine the same questions from different perspectives.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum consistently studies society and power through history, philosophy, politics, sociology, law and cultural analysis, so the label captures its central organising fields.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces most economics, natural-science, ecology, health and psychology study with a denser sequence in law, international relations, political thought, history, literature, media and cultural analysis.
progression: Introductory law, politics, literary analysis and history support later work on international law, conflict, identity and public debate. Qualitative methods and art history precede the final research courses.
traceOverrides: introduces sociological analysis of institutions, identities, inequality and social interaction
compares political institutions and systems using concepts and empirical evidence
examines political, social and cultural transformations in modern history
examines how public communication frames knowledge, responsibility and collective action through the climate crisis

alternatives.label: Life, mind & health
alternatives.concept: Connect cells, genes and physiology with how people perceive, develop and respond to illness. Combine laboratory work and neuroscience with psychology, epidemiology and statistical research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains integrated biological, biomedical, neuroscientific, psychological and public-health sequences, so the label accurately identifies life, mind and health as its three connected domains.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with both earlier alternatives, this route replaces most humanities, politics, law, culture and sustainability study with a sequenced laboratory, life-science, biomedical, neuroscience, psychology and health curriculum.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes psycholinguistics, perception and higher cognition. Introductory statistics precedes experimental analysis and research synthesis. Foundations in biomedicine, biochemistry and physiology support laboratory work, pharmacology and disease study.
traceOverrides: provides foundations in cells, physiology, health and biomedical science
introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of brain and behaviour

routeSelection.route: Bachelor of Arts with an interdomain Humanities and Social Sciences major
routeSelection.basis: The generic UCU target does not specify BA/BSc, domain or discipline. The formally available Humanities-and-Social-Sciences interdomain BA major most directly represents UCU's broad interdisciplinary academic identity and the programme overview's cross-disciplinary social and cultural examples. Exact tracks remain student choices; the route was selected before and independently of UCR course selection.

selection.assessment: Two coherent generator-backed directions beyond the broad closest match are feasible and substantively distinct: society, power and culture; and life, mind and health. Both materially change the curriculum and exceed the pairwise 30-EC floor. The maximum of three alternatives is therefore reached; environment and sustainability, economics and social analysis, and mathematics and physical science remain coherent assessed directions but cannot be added.

blocks: Both first-year courses develop research questions, evidence evaluation and written argument. UCR also emphasises personal and professional development.
UCR covers interviews, observation and qualitative analysis, which overlap with UCU’s qualitative option. UCU also allows other methods depending on the thesis discipline.
Both introduce empirical research design and statistical analysis. UCU teaches them in a social-science context.
UCU requires a 15 EC thesis within the major. The optional 15 EC UCR research element sits outside the course schedules.

notes.text: Both colleges offer interdisciplinary Liberal Arts and Sciences. The UCU example shows an interdomain BA with disciplinary tracks, methods in both domains, and a required thesis. The UCR columns show three course schedules. At UCR, a cluster-specific major depends on the courses completed.

audience.programmeDescription: University College Utrecht offers a Liberal Arts and Sciences degree across Humanities, Science and Social Sciences. This example shows a BA major combining Humanities and Social Sciences.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR examples combine society, culture and science, focus on power and institutions, or explore life science, cognition and health.
